sunday.lead: Nvidia lost a quarter of its value in about a month. Coverage this week pointed to three causes, each feeding into the next.

email.teaser: Sunday's report: the three reasons Nvidia lost $1.4T, Friday's bounce, and the bull vs. bear case before Nov 17.

causes.title: Data-center pushback
causes.text: Calls to halt new data centers raised a simple question: will the world need as many chips? Shares slipped under $200 for the first time since August.

causes.title: Pricier money
causes.text: The US added 165K jobs against roughly 70K expected. A strong labor market put a rate hike back on the table, and higher rates make data-center builds costlier to fund.

causes.title: Buyers in debt
causes.text: CoreWeave, one of Nvidia's big customers, carries $35B of debt. AI builders are burning cash to buy chips, which makes Nvidia's own buyers look shakier.

after_causes.title: Then Friday
after_causes.text: Chips bounced during Friday's session, with Nvidia up about 6% and the chip index up about 4%. These were intraday moves, not closing prices.

email.next_text: One date matters most: Nvidia reports on Tuesday, Nov 17. The figure to watch is the $108B guide. History is mixed: the stock fell after 6 of its last 10 reports.
